surfaces.note: The Stable 1.x language core is the ordinary fully implemented source subset covered by the permanent 1.0 conformance corpus: lexical structure; primitive scalar types and literals; functions; const/local bindings; structs/enums where covered; fixed arrays; ordinary expressions/casts; if/else, while and for; return/break/continue; imports/exports required by Stable compilation; and the C FFI subset covered by conformance/integration tests. Implementation status alone does not promote an advanced/domain surface into this compatibility class.

Advanced or incompletely qualified surfaces remain outside the initial 1.x source-compatibility promise until individually promoted. This includes partial match forms, module-block namespacing, backend-specific test/dbg/expect semantics, UI layout sugar, specialised safety/profile attributes not in the Stable corpus, and other spec entries marked partial.

Effects ship and are exercised, but the default unhandled-effect coverage/failure policy tracked by #563/#643 is not frozen for 1.0. The subsystem may be promoted to Stable in a compatible 1.x release once normal compilation fails loudly and its continuation boundary is fully qualified.
flow/evolution, dsys and related domain DSLs remain usable but outside the initial 1.x compatibility promise. In particular, #631 must be resolved before dsys promotion to Stable.
Verification and proof syntax may change during 1.x until explicitly promoted.
Abort, retry and multi-shot continuation capture are outside the shipped tail-resumptive model unless implemented and promoted later.

Only foundational public APIs explicitly exercised by the Stable conformance/integration corpus are covered by the 1.x stdlib promise. Stable status attaches to documented covered symbols, not automatically to every symbol in a file under lib/stdlib.

Domain, numerical, autodiff, AI, audio, graphics, GPU, concurrency, crypto, networking, dynamics/control and other specialised stdlib modules ship as Experimental unless an individual API is explicitly promoted into stdlib-core.

Flow 1.0 makes a source-compatibility and documented C-interop promise, not a general cross-version binary ABI promise for compiler-generated/internal runtime layouts. Explicit exported C symbols and representations documented as Stable remain governed by their focused FFI contract.
Stable 1.x core: help, version, C compile/run and test; flow run propagates the executed program's exit status.

flow fmt remains Experimental in 1.0. The current formatter does not yet round-trip the full Stable grammar; promotion requires deterministic/idempotent parse-format-parse qualification without dropping declarations or changing semantics.
Specialised backends, graphics/audio/debug tooling, advanced compiler commands, formatter and package/native workflows remain outside the Stable CLI promise unless separately promoted.
Stable project core: package name/version/entry, string path aliases, upward manifest discovery and forward-compatible unknown extensions.
Dependency acquisition/source forms, dev dependencies, native linking, publication metadata and development-policy tables remain Experimental pending package/security qualification.

The portable C backend is the production backend for the Stable language core. Final v1.0.0 publication remains blocked until Tier-1 platform/toolchain and release-artifact qualification pass; classification states the compatibility contract, not that qualification has already completed.
Optional backend/toolchain; does not define 1.0 Stable semantics.
